[reference generation] A 10-second cinematic AMV sequence of two characters infiltrating a volcanic industrial refinery to disable the core reactor and escape. Characters are taken from <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>, environment from <Picture 4>, and shot order + path from <Picture 1>.

<Subject 3> (appears in all shots): fully_preserved - architecture, lava glow, industrial density and lighting from <Picture 4> are retained as the continuous environment.

detailed_description:
Cinematic, dark industrial sci-fi, high-detail digital illustration style matching the reference concept art, dramatic orange lava glow against deep shadows and steam.

[Shot 1] A wide establishing shot of <Subject 3> at sunset. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> stand at the outer edge of the industrial perimeter, observing the massive glowing refinery and its molten core from a distance. Camera holds a static wide shot as they assess the structure, silhouetted against the rising smoke and lava light. Tension is high — the mission has not yet begun.

[Shot 2] At 00:01.800, the shot cuts to a frontal tracking shot on the upper ring of <Subject 3>. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> run directly toward the camera along narrow maintenance walkways and pipes high above the lava channels. <Subject 1> is slightly ahead and to the left, <Subject 2> close beside her on the right, both facing the camera. The camera tracks backward at medium-fast speed, then smoothly arcs and circles around them to the side, finally settling into a tracking shot from behind as they continue running toward the core. Steam and sparks whip past throughout the continuous camera move. This shot continues longer as they cover distance across the ring.

[Shot 3] At 00:05.800, the shot cuts to the reactor core interior of <Subject 3>. Intense molten light floods the frame. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> reach the central control console. <Subject 2> plants the large ornate key into the mechanism while <Subject 1> covers him, both silhouetted against the roaring core. Camera holds a tense medium-wide shot as sparks fly and the core begins to destabilize.

[Shot 4] At 00:08.000, the shot cuts to a wide establishing shot of <Subject 3> under darkening sky and rising smoke, framed similarly to Shot 1. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> stand at a safe distance on the outer edge after successfully disabling the core, looking back at the now-unstable, violently glowing and smoking refinery. Camera holds a static wide shot as they catch their breath, the mission complete. The atmosphere is one of hard-won relief rather than tension.

overall_soundscape: Heavy industrial ambience of roaring furnaces, hissing steam, and metallic creaks from the structure. Distant alarms begin after the core breach. Footsteps on metal grating, fabric movement, and the sharp metallic click of the key engaging the console. Rising low rumble as the reactor destabilizes, then settling into a lower, more distant industrial drone in the final shot.

non_diegetic_music: Driving industrial electronic pulse with deep sub-bass and sparse metallic percussion, building in intensity through the core breach then cutting to a tense sparse rhythm for the escape, resolving into a lower, more subdued pulse in the final shot.

nodes.title: READ ME - LTX-2.5 2x
widgets_values:
LTX-2.5 LATENT SPATIAL x2 (24GB)
The 22B IC-LoRA pixel pass OOMs on a 24GB laptop: the
transformer alone stages 20.5GB, then the first sample
step asks for another 1.1GB. Official LTX low-VRAM target
for that path is 32GB.

This subgraph uses the official LTX-2.5 latent spatial x2
upsampler instead: MiniMax pixels -> LTX VAE encode ->
latent x2 -> tiled decode. No 22B, no Gemma, no 8-step
sample. Audio stays MiniMax.

Frames are cropped to 8n+1 for the LTX VAE.
Toggle Upscaler (LTX-2.5 2x) to skip. RTX is separate.

Model:
  latent_upscale_models/ltx/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors
  vae/ltx-2.5/ltx-2.5-video-vae-conv-bf16.safetensors

nodes.title: READ ME - Post Grade
widgets_values:
POST GRADE + PIPELINE FIXES (v4)
Created using Anthropic Claude - keep this note on internal versions
until the settings have been reviewed/verified.

PATH:
  VAEDecode -> LTX-2.5 latent spatial x2 -> Grade
    -> Interpolation -> Sharpen -> VideoCombine
LTX must stay before interpolation.

The grade used to sit after interpolation, so it processed every
interpolated frame (124 -> 616 with RIFE alone, ~4900 with all three
stacked). It now runs on the 124 decoded frames. The last-frame save
for shot chaining is also taken post-grade, so the next shot starts
from a colour-matched frame.

ONE INTERPOLATOR AT A TIME. They chain in series, so enabling two
multiplies: RIFE 5x * GMFSS 4x * FILM 2x = 40x the frames and an
8x audio/video desync. v3 shipped with all three live - that was
the performance collapse. The parent "Frame Interpolation" group
was deleted because toggling it re-enabled all three at once; the
three child groups are now brown and appear in the main toggler,
with "max one" enforced by the small bypasser next to them.

FPS and frames share the same switch order (first live wins):
  any_01 GMFSS   96  (4x). Unused interpolators must be MUTED, not bypassed.
  any_02 FILM    48  (2x). Bypass passes original frames through and a 96fps
  any_03 RIFE   120  (5x). file of those frames plays in ~1s.
  any_04 original / base 24
Change a multiplier -> change the matching fps primitive.

RIFE flow scale is 1.0. It was 4.0, which computes optical flow at
4x resolution for roughly 16x the cost with no benefit at 544p.
Try 2.0 if you want more accurate flow and can pay for it.

Grade is still BYPASSED and lut_file is "None" - nothing is being
graded right now. Enable the Post Grade group and pick
Worlds_AMV_Style.cube to get the look back.

Output is h264 / yuv420p 8-bit / crf 16. For the HDR grade, enable
the Master Export (h265, yuv420p10le, crf 12) instead - 8-bit will
band the shadow rolloff.

GRADE TUNING (change one at a time):
 1 Pseudo-HDR  hdr_intensity 0.45. Above ~0.8 goes haloed.
 2 LUT         strength 0.7. 0.4-0.5 if skin goes too gold.
 3 Trim        saturation/contrast +10-15 finishing pass.
 4 Bloom       intensity 0; most memory-hungry stage here.
 5 Sharpen     alpha 0.35 subtle, 0.6+ crunchy. Stays after the
               upscaler so it works at final resolution.

Requires Worlds_AMV_Style.cube in ComfyUI/models/luts/ and
colour-science in python_embeded. The LUT is an algorithmic
approximation of the Riot Worlds look, not an official Riot asset.
